beats.text: In September 1933, ten men broke out of the Indiana State Prison in Michigan City. The guns had been smuggled in.
beats.label: MICHIGAN CITY, INDIANA

beats.text: John Dillinger, paroled from that prison in May, helped plan it, and had pistols hidden in a shipment to the prison's shirt shop.
beats.label: THE PLAN
beats.credit: PBS American Experience; Britannica; History.com; Purvis (1938)

beats.text: By then, Dillinger was locked up again himself, arrested in Dayton, Ohio, four days earlier.
beats.label: SEPT. 22, 1933
beats.credit: Wright State University; Encyclopedia of Indianapolis

beats.text: On September 26, the ten forced their way out at gunpoint, shooting a prison clerk. They took a visiting sheriff hostage and fled in commandeered cars.
beats.label: SEPT. 26, 1933

beats.text: Two weeks later, three of them walked into the jail in Lima, Ohio, posing as Indiana officers, and freed Dillinger. Sheriff Jess Sarber was shot, and died that night.
beats.label: LIMA, OHIO, OCT. 12, 1933
beats.credit: Allen County Sheriff's Office; PBS; Lima News

beats.text: The gang lasted less than a year. Federal agents killed Dillinger in Chicago in July 1934, and Harry Pierpont was executed that October.
beats.credit: U.S. Census Bureau; FBI; Indiana Historical Bureau

beats.text: The prison in Michigan City, near the lakefront, dates to 1860, and it still holds inmates today, so view it from the road.
beats.label: INDIANA STATE PRISON

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

end_card.pill: Tonight: Dillinger at Crown Point's old jail

factcheck.result: Lines 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 supported. Changed: line 4 to 'forced their way out at gunpoint, shooting a prison clerk' and 'a visiting sheriff' (Sheriff Neel of Harrison County); line 7 'near the lakefront' instead of 'on the lakeshore'.
